articles.title: CPU Bottleneck Explained: How to Tell if Your Processor Is Holding Back Your Games
articles.excerpt: A CPU bottleneck means your processor, not your graphics card, is limiting frame rate. How to check in a few minutes and what to do about it.
articles.hero_image_alt: Illustration of a PC limited by the processor at 1080p and by the graphics card at 4K

body.text: A CPU bottleneck happens when your processor cannot prepare frames as fast as your graphics card can draw them. **The sign is a graphics card that is not working at full load while your frame rate is lower than you want.**
How to check

items: Start a game and open a monitoring overlay. The Xbox Game Bar (Windows + G) shows processor and graphics card usage.
Play a busy section for a few minutes.
Look at the graphics card usage.

rows: The graphics card is the limit. This is normal.
Graphics card usage well below 100%, frame rate low
The processor is likely the limit.
Graphics card usage well below 100%, frame rate at your cap
Nothing is wrong. A frame limit is holding it there.

body.text: Do not judge by overall processor usage alone. A game can be held back by one or two busy cores while the total looks low.
Why resolution changes the answer
At lower resolutions the graphics card finishes each frame quickly, so the processor becomes the limit. At higher resolutions the graphics card has more work to do and becomes the limit.
That is why the same PC can be processor-limited at 1080p and graphics-limited at 4K.
What you can do

items: **Raise the resolution or graphics settings.** If the processor is the limit, this costs few frames and makes the game look better.
**Lower processor-heavy settings.** Crowd density, draw distance and physics detail load the processor more than the graphics card.
**Close background apps,** especially browsers with many tabs.
**Check your memory is running at its rated speed.** See [DDR4 vs DDR5 for gaming](/memory/ddr4-vs-ddr5-gaming) for how memory profiles work.

body.text: When to upgrade the processor

Consider it when you are processor-limited in the games you play most, at the settings you want, and the steps above have not helped. Check which processors your motherboard supports first. A newer processor for the same socket is far cheaper than replacing the motherboard and memory as well.
A bottleneck is not a fault
Every PC has a limiting part in every game. It only matters when the frame rate is lower than you want.

articles.title: Monitor Refresh Rate Explained: 60 Hz, 144 Hz and 240 Hz for Gaming
articles.excerpt: Refresh rate is how many times per second a monitor updates. What 60, 144 and 240 Hz mean in practice, and why your graphics card has to keep up.
articles.hero_image_alt: Chart of time between new pictures at 60 Hz, 144 Hz and 240 Hz

body.text: Refresh rate is the number of times your monitor updates the picture each second, measured in hertz. **A 144 Hz monitor can show up to 144 frames per second, but only if your PC produces that many.**
What each refresh rate means

rows: Most players. A clear step up in smoothness
Competitive shooters with a strong PC

body.text: Your graphics card has to keep up
A high refresh rate only helps when your frame rate is high as well. If your PC runs a game at 70 frames per second, a 240 Hz monitor shows 70 frames per second.
Before buying, check what frame rate you get in the games you play. Many games have a frame counter in their settings, and Steam can show one in its overlay.
The jump that matters most
Going from 60 Hz to 144 Hz is the change most people notice straight away. Going from 144 Hz to 240 Hz is a smaller step, and you need a much faster PC to make use of it.
Variable refresh rate

Frame rates move up and down while you play. **Variable refresh rate** lets the monitor match its updates to the frames your graphics card sends, which removes screen tearing. It is sold as **G-Sync** by Nvidia and **FreeSync** by AMD, and many monitors work with both.
It is worth having on any gaming monitor, and most models now include it.
Resolution comes into it too
A higher resolution is harder to run. The same graphics card produces fewer frames at 1440p than at 1080p, and fewer again at 4K. Pick the resolution and refresh rate together:

items: **1080p at 144 Hz** suits mid-range graphics cards.
**1440p at 144 Hz** is a good balance for stronger cards.
**4K at high refresh rates** needs a high-end card.

body.text: To see which cards new games ask for, read [what graphics card October 2026's big PC games need](/gpu/october-2026-games-gpu-requirements).
Turn it on in Windows

A new monitor often starts at 60 Hz. Open **Settings**, then **System**, **Display**, **Advanced display**, and choose the highest refresh rate. Use a DisplayPort cable or a recent HDMI cable, because older cables can limit the refresh rate.

articles.title: NVMe vs SATA SSD for Gaming: Does the Faster Drive Matter?
articles.excerpt: New games require an SSD, but not always the fastest one. How SATA and NVMe drives compare, what the PS5 needs, and which to buy for a gaming PC.
articles.hero_image_alt: Chart comparing top speeds of hard drives, SATA SSDs and NVMe SSDs

body.text: **Any SSD is a big step up from a hard drive, and many new games now require one.** An NVMe drive is faster than a SATA SSD on paper, but in most games today the difference in loading times is small.
How the drive types compare
These are the fastest sequential speeds each type is built for. Real game loading depends on much more than this one number.
What games actually require
Official requirements for new releases often say just "SSD required" without naming a type. Ace Combat 8, Modern Warfare 4 and Phantom Blade Zero all list an SSD. A SATA SSD meets that requirement.
Where NVMe helps

items: **Copying and installing large games** is much quicker.
**Games built around fast storage** can load and stream data faster on NVMe.
**Price:** NVMe drives now often cost about the same as SATA drives of the same size, so there is little reason to choose SATA for a new build.

body.text: What to buy

items: **New PC or new drive:** buy an NVMe drive if your motherboard has an M.2 slot. A PCIe 4.0 drive is the sensible choice for most people.
**Older PC with no M.2 slot:** a SATA SSD is still a large upgrade over a hard drive.
**PCIe 5.0 drives** cost more and need good cooling. Games do not need them today.

body.text: For PlayStation 5 owners
The PS5's expansion slot takes an M.2 NVMe drive. Sony asks for a PCIe 4.0 drive with a read speed of 5,500 MB/s or faster, and recommends one with a heatsink.
How much space
New games are large. Modern Warfare 4 lists 115 GB and Ace Combat 8 lists 125 GB. A 1 TB drive fills up quickly, so 2 TB is worth considering if you keep several big games installed.
Storage is one part of the picture. For memory, see [16 GB vs 32 GB of RAM for gaming](/memory/16gb-vs-32gb-ram-gaming).

articles.title: DDR4 vs DDR5 for Gaming: Which One Does Your PC Use?
articles.excerpt: DDR4 and DDR5 memory are not interchangeable. Which AMD and Intel platforms use which type, and what to check before buying more RAM.
articles.hero_image_alt: Table of AMD and Intel platforms and the memory type each one uses

body.text: **You cannot choose between DDR4 and DDR5 freely. Your motherboard decides.** The two types have different slots, so a DDR5 stick will not fit a DDR4 board and the other way round.
Which platforms use which memory

rows: DDR4 or DDR5, depending on the motherboard

body.text: On Intel LGA1700, each motherboard model supports one type only. Check the board's name or manual before buying.
How to check what you have now

items: Open **Task Manager**, go to the **Performance** tab and select **Memory**. The speed and slots used are shown there, and many systems show the type in the top corner.
Or look up your motherboard model on the maker's website. The memory type is listed in the specifications.

body.text: Is DDR5 faster for games?
DDR5 runs at higher speeds, and that can help frame rates in games that lean hard on the processor. For most players the difference is smaller than the gain from a better graphics card.
So the practical advice is simple:

items: **Upgrading an existing PC:** buy more of the type your board already uses.
**Building a new PC:** current AMD and Intel platforms use DDR5, so that is what you will buy.

body.text: Turn on the memory profile

New memory often runs at a slower default speed until you enable its profile in the motherboard settings. The profile is called **XMP** on Intel kits and **EXPO** on AMD kits. Without it you may not get the speed printed on the box.
How much to buy
See [16 GB vs 32 GB of RAM for gaming](/memory/16gb-vs-32gb-ram-gaming) for what new games actually ask for.

articles.title: What Power Supply Wattage Do You Need for a Gaming PC?
articles.excerpt: Recommended power supply sizes for RTX 50 series graphics cards, from 650 W to 1000 W, and how to check your own PSU before a GPU upgrade.
articles.hero_image_alt: Chart of recommended power supply wattage for RTX 5070, 5070 Ti, 5080 and 5090

body.text: Your graphics card decides most of your power supply needs. For Nvidia's RTX 50 series, the usual recommendations run from **650 W for an RTX 5070** to **1000 W for an RTX 5090**.
Recommended PSU size by graphics card
These are whole-system recommendations with a typical gaming CPU. Always confirm on the product page for your exact card, because some models from board makers ask for more.
Why the number is higher than the card's own power draw

A power supply has to cover the whole PC, and graphics cards draw short bursts well above their rated power. Seasonic notes that the RTX 5090 is rated at 575 W, while independent testing has recorded very brief spikes far higher. The recommended wattage leaves room for those bursts.
How to check the PSU you already have

items: Look for the label on the side of the power supply. It lists the total wattage.
If you bought a pre-built PC, check the maker's spec sheet for your model.
Do not rely on the efficiency badge. An 80 PLUS rating tells you how efficient the unit is, not how many watts it delivers.

body.text: Check the power connector too

RTX 50 series cards use a 16-pin power connector called **12V-2x6**. Newer power supplies built to the ATX 3.1 standard have this cable built in. With an older PSU you use the adapter that comes with the card.
Push the connector in fully until it clicks, and avoid bending the cable sharply right at the plug.
Do you need to replace your PSU?

items: **Your PSU meets the recommended wattage and is a few years old:** you are fine.
**It is 100 W or more below the recommendation:** replace it before installing the new card.
**You do not know the brand or it came with a very cheap case:** treat it as a risk and replace it.

body.text: A power supply is not the part to save money on. A failing one can take other components with it.
Not sure which card you need? See [what graphics card October 2026's big PC games need](/gpu/october-2026-games-gpu-requirements).
Sources

items: [Seasonic, how to calculate PSU power for RTX 50 series GPUs](https://seasonic.com/insights/how-to-calculate-psu-power-for-rtx-5090-gpus/)

articles.title: 16 GB vs 32 GB of RAM for Gaming: What New Games Actually Ask For
articles.excerpt: 16 GB of RAM still meets the recommended tier of most new games, but two October 2026 releases ask for 32 GB in their higher tiers. Here is how to decide.
articles.hero_image_alt: Table of minimum and recommended RAM for five October 2026 games

body.text: **16 GB of RAM is still enough for most new games**, but 32 GB is starting to appear in official requirements. Of five big October 2026 releases we checked, two ask for 32 GB in a higher tier.
What five new games ask for
When 16 GB is fine

items: You play at the minimum or recommended tier of most games.
You close your browser and other apps while playing.
You are on a tight budget and your money is better spent on the graphics card.

body.text: When 32 GB is worth it

items: A game you want lists it, as Ace Combat 8 does for its recommended tier.
You keep a browser, chat apps or streaming software open while you play.
You are building a new PC and want it to last several years.

body.text: 8 GB is no longer enough
Only one of these five games lists 8 GB, and only as its minimum. If you have 8 GB, upgrading memory is one of the cheapest ways to make new games playable.
Before you buy more RAM

items: **Check which type your motherboard uses.** DDR4 and DDR5 are not interchangeable. See [DDR4 vs DDR5 for gaming](/memory/ddr4-vs-ddr5-gaming).
**Buy a matched kit of two sticks.** Two sticks run in dual-channel mode, which is faster than one stick of the same total size.
**Avoid mixing old and new kits if you can.** Different kits do not always run reliably together at their rated speed.

articles.title: What Graphics Card Do October 2026's Big PC Games Need?
articles.excerpt: We compared the official PC requirements of five October 2026 releases. The RTX 2060 is the most common minimum, the RTX 3060 Ti the most recommended.
articles.hero_image_alt: Table of minimum and recommended graphics cards for five October 2026 games

body.text: We lined up the official PC requirements of five big October 2026 releases. Two cards keep coming up: the **RTX 2060** as the minimum and the **RTX 3060 Ti** as the recommended card.
The requirements side by side

rows: RTX 3060 Ti / RX 6700 XT / Arc B580
RTX 3060 Ti / RX 6600 XT / Arc B580

body.text: What the pattern tells you

items: **The RTX 2060 is the minimum in three of the five games.** If your card is older or slower than that, expect to be below the official minimum for much of this season.
**The RTX 3060 Ti is recommended in three of the five.** It is the closest thing to a "safe" card for this group of games at 1080p and 1440p.
**AMD's RX 6700 XT appears next to the RTX 3060 Ti twice.** That is the Radeon to compare against.
**Intel Arc is now listed by name.** The A580 shows up as a minimum three times and the B580 as a recommendation twice.

body.text: Read the small print on resolution

Recommended does not mean the same thing in every game. Ace Combat 8's recommended tier targets 1080p at 60 FPS on Medium with upscaling. Phantom Blade Zero's targets 1440p at 60 FPS with upscaling. Always check the resolution and frame rate each tier is aiming for.
If you want ray tracing
The ray tracing tiers ask for much newer cards:

rows: RTX 5060 for ray tracing at 1080p, RTX 5080 for path tracing at 4K

body.text: What to do with this

items: **Have an RTX 3060 Ti, RX 6700 XT or better?** You meet the recommended tier for most of these games.
**Have an RTX 2060 or similar?** You can run most of them at minimum settings. Plan for Low to Medium at 1080p.
**Have a GTX 10-series card or older?** Two of these games still list cards that old, but most do not.

body.text: Memory matters too. Two of these games ask for 32 GB of RAM in their higher tiers. See [16 GB vs 32 GB of RAM for gaming](/memory/16gb-vs-32gb-ram-gaming).

articles.title: RTX 60 Series Release Date: Why Leaks Now Point to 2028
articles.excerpt: Nvidia has not announced the RTX 60 series. Several leakers now say it has slipped to 2028. What was reported, by whom, and what to do if you need a GPU now.
articles.hero_image_alt: Timeline of leaked next-generation graphics card timing: no new Nvidia generation in 2026, one AMD chip in 2027, RTX 60 series in 2028

body.text: **Nvidia has not announced the RTX 60 series or a release date for it.** In September 2026, several well-known hardware leakers said the next GeForce generation has slipped to **2028**. Everything below about timing is **rumor**, not confirmed information.
What is confirmed and what is rumor

rows: Nvidia has announced the RTX 60 series
Nvidia launched a new gaming GPU generation in 2026
Most of AMD's next Radeon generation also arrives in 2028
One AMD chip, known as AT2, arrives in 2027

body.text: Who said what

items: **Kepler_L2**, posting on the AnandTech forums in mid-September 2026, said nearly all of Nvidia's and AMD's next-generation cards are now expected in 2028. The exception was an AMD chip codenamed AT2, said to be on track for 2027. TechSpot and PCGamesN reported the post.
**Kopite7kimi**, another long-running leaker, said a few days later that the RTX 60 series had been postponed again, also pointing to 2028.
An earlier rumor from a different source had suggested the first half of 2027.

body.text: Leakers have been right and wrong before. Until Nvidia says something, treat 2028 as the current best guess and nothing more.
Why it might be delayed
The explanation given in these reports is demand for AI hardware. Data center chips are far more profitable than gaming cards, and both compete for the same manufacturing capacity and memory.
PCGamesN's report links the timing to a squeeze on the memory used in graphics cards, which is being prioritised for AI products.
What this means if you need a graphics card now

items: **Do not wait for the RTX 60 series.** If the leaks are right, it is more than a year away. If they are wrong, nobody knows by how much.

**Buy for the games you play today.** The official requirements of this season's releases are a better guide than rumors. See [what graphics card October 2026's big PC games need](/gpu/october-2026-games-gpu-requirements).
**Check your power supply before upgrading.** See [what power supply wattage you need](/power/psu-wattage-for-gaming-pc).

body.text: What to watch for
Nvidia usually reveals new generations at its own events or at trade shows. An official announcement, not a forum post, is what will settle the date. We will update this page if one comes.
Sources

items: [TechSpot, Nvidia and AMD next gaming GPUs could be delayed until 2028](https://www.techspot.com/news/113874-nvidia-amd-next-gaming-gpus-could-delayed-until.html)
[PCGamesN, next generation of AMD and Nvidia GPUs rumored for 2028 launch](https://www.pcgamesn.com/nvidia/amd-next-gen-gpus-2028-rumor)

articles.title: DLSS 5 Explained: Which Graphics Cards and Games Support It
articles.excerpt: DLSS 5 launched on September 3, 2026 in NBA 2K27 and works on GeForce RTX 50 series cards. What it does, which games are confirmed and what it does not do.
articles.hero_image_alt: DLSS 5 status: released September 3, 2026, works on RTX 50 series, available in NBA 2K27

body.text: **DLSS 5 is available now, in one game, on GeForce RTX 50 series graphics cards.** It launched on September 3, 2026 in NBA 2K27. Unlike earlier versions, its main job is to improve how a game looks, not to raise the frame rate.
DLSS 5 at a glance

rows: GeForce RTX 50 series, desktop and laptop

body.text: What DLSS 5 does
Earlier versions of DLSS are mainly about performance. They render the game at a lower resolution and rebuild a sharper picture, or generate extra frames.

DLSS 5 adds what Nvidia calls **neural rendering**. It uses the frame your game produces, plus data from the game engine, to produce a final image with more convincing lighting and materials. It works alongside the game's normal rendering and does not replace it.
So the short version is: DLSS 4 is mostly about more frames, and DLSS 5 is mostly about a better-looking picture.
Which graphics cards support DLSS 5
Nvidia's compatibility list shows **GeForce RTX 50 series** cards. RTX 40, 30 and 20 series cards are not marked as supporting it.
Older RTX cards keep the DLSS features they already have, such as Super Resolution. Nvidia has not announced DLSS 5 for them, so do not assume it will arrive later.
Which games support DLSS 5
**Right now: NBA 2K27.** In that game the option is called DLSS Neural Rendering and sits in the video settings.
Nvidia has also named a first group of games that will get it. None of these had it at the time of writing:

items: AION 2
Assassin's Creed Shadows
Black State
Cinder City
Delta Force
Hogwarts Legacy
Justice
Naraka: Bladepoint
NTE: Neverness to Everness
Phantom Blade Zero
Resident Evil Requiem
Sea of Remnants
Starfield
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
Where Winds Meet

body.text: A game that supports DLSS 4.5 does not automatically support DLSS 5. Each game needs its own update.
The debate about it

Because DLSS 5 changes lighting and materials, some players and developers have said it can make characters and scenes look different from what the artists intended. Early footage of Resident Evil Requiem drew that criticism.
It is a setting you can turn off, so you can compare and decide for yourself.
Should you buy an RTX 50 card for DLSS 5?
Not for this feature alone. One game supports it today. Choose a graphics card on its performance, memory and price in the games you play, and count DLSS 5 as a bonus.
For what new games ask for, see [what graphics card October 2026's big PC games need](/gpu/october-2026-games-gpu-requirements).
Quick answers
Is DLSS 5 out?
Yes, since September 3, 2026, in NBA 2K27.
Does DLSS 5 work on RTX 40 series cards?
Nvidia's list shows only RTX 50 series cards.
Does DLSS 5 increase FPS?
That is not its purpose. It is designed to improve image quality.
